Bead ddx-096129b9 asks for watchdog reap to route through the same managed-tree
cleanup helper Stop uses, with a process-tree test proving watchdog reap
follows SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL and releases the claimed bead.

This work already landed in commit 341fa83f6f "fix: reap managed watchdog
trees [ddx-3e734740]", which is an ancestor of this bead's base-rev
(f3461e2cb384a2e8506a602ea653eb836b5c2517). Verified directly against the
current worktree, not just the commit message:

- cli/internal/server/workers.go:2133-2204 (reapWorker) calls
  cleanupManagedWorkerProcessTree(processRoot, cleanupPGIDs, grace) — the
  identical helper Stop calls at workers.go:1794-1798 — with the same
  cleanupPGIDs slice and watchdog kill-grace deadline.
- reapWorker emits the bead.reaped event and releases the claim (Unclaim)
  before touching the process tree, and flips state=reaped + persists,
  matching Stop's ordering.
- Idempotency: watchdogSweep sets handle.reaped=true under the manager lock
  before invoking reapWorker, so a worker can only be picked once per sweep
  cycle and repeated sweeps skip already-reaped handles.
- cli/internal/server/workers_watchdog_test.go:520 already defines
  TestManagedWorkerWatchdogReapKillsProcessTree exactly as named in AC #1,
  spawning a managed process tree (root/claude/claude-sleep/codex/codex-sleep),
  forcing a stall, and asserting: state flips to "reaped", cleanup escalates
  to SIGKILL (lastError contains "sigkill="), the bead claim is released
  (status=open), exactly one bead.reaped event is recorded, and every
  descendant process is gone.

Ran the verification command above: PASS (0.71s), no failures.

No source changes were needed, so no commit was made. AC #3 (make install)
and AC #4 (lefthook run pre-commit) are gated on a code change landing;
since this bead requires none, they do not apply.
